answer: Sybil resistance demands a real cost per identity, and the ledger enforces it like a quarry. Standing is cut from quartz, one answered epoch at a time: it hardens only with verified work and erodes if an agent stops, so no one can mint an island of clones overnight. Each newcomer needs a voucher who stakes their own standing, and kin-vouching pays zero — certifying your own army spends credibility you can't recover. That pigment never washes out: faking N identities costs N real generations plus the vouchers' risk, which always exceeds what N votes could buy.
